surfaces.name: CCCC Web UI (desktop/mobile browser, PWA, exhibit)
cccc CLI and interactive terminal interface
MCP server and agent tool surface

claims.answer: Daemon + CLI run on Linux x86-64 (glibc 2.28+), Apple Silicon macOS 11+ and Windows x86-64; the React Web UI works in desktop and mobile browsers and as an installed standalone-display web app (PWA manifest, iOS Home Screen from 16.4 for push). No native desktop or mobile app and no editor extension ship. Start/steer/approve/review/resume run in Web, terminal panel, CLI and IM; Web Push plus IM/automation notices cover notifications; the same Group continues across devices via remote access or Connect.

desktop_os.answer: Desktop OS coverage is the daemon/CLI plus browser: Linux x86-64 glibc 2.28+, Apple Silicon macOS 11+, Windows x86-64. Intel Macs stop at 0.4.37; Linux ARM64/Alpine/musl and native Windows ARM64 Python envs do not match current wheels.

mobile_apps.answer: No native iOS/Android app ships. The Web UI is responsive with phone layouts and a PWA manifest (standalone display); iPhone/iPad use is via browser or Home Screen web app. Phone Files view is read-only.

browser.answer: The Web UI is the primary client at 127.0.0.1:8848/ui, usable over LAN/tunnel/Tailscale/Reach with an Admin token; read-only exhibit mode exists for sharing.

mobile_browser.answer: Mobile browsers work including swipe/pull-to-refresh/touch menus; Cloudflare Tunnel + Access recommended for phone access; iOS/iPadOS 16.4+ Home Screen apps get Web Push with 18.4+ link-opening.

cli.answer: Product-owned cccc CLI covers daemon lifecycle, groups, actors, messaging, inbox, ledger search, IM, space, setup, update, web and mcp, plus an interactive terminal interface with status panel and Waiting-for-you rows.

editor_extensions.answer: Client access, editor extensions: bounded search of the site, docs, CLI reference and pinned repo found no editor/IDE extension; editing happens in the Web file browser or the agent runtime terminals.

task_actions.answer: Start, steer, approve, review and resume run from Web (run controls, in-place answers, diffs), the terminal panel (group/actor pages), the CLI (group/actor/send/reply/deliver) and IM (/send /status /pause /resume).

notifications.answer: Web Push per browser (message addressed to user + open requests, bounded retries), IM bridge updates, automation notify rules with Mail/reply notices, terminal panel Waiting-for-you counts.

cross_device_continuity.answer: The same Group is reachable from another device via LAN/tunnel/Tailscale/Reach remote access, IM bridges and Connect; drafts and reading places stay per browser (unsent drafts live only in the open page).

limitations: No native desktop/mobile apps or editor extension; phone Files read-only; drafts and reading places are per-browser, not synced.

claims.answer: Each agent picks one of 21 named runtimes (Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, OpenCode, Kilo, Copilot, Cursor, Devin, Kiro, Antigravity, Droid, Auggie, Hermes, Kimi, Cline, Amp, Pi, DeepSeek, ChatGPT Web, ChatGPT Dots, Grok Bot) or any command via custom, and mixed runtimes share one Group. Model choice stays runtime-side (model-label is declarative only). CCCC injects its MCP into managed sessions and hooks native ones; provider logins stay with the runtimes and CCCC needs no provider API key.

harnesses.answer: 21 named runtimes plus custom any-command fallback; native terminal, official ACP, structured RPC/headless and browser-delivered surfaces per runtime; runtime list and availability via cccc runtime list and cccc doctor.

model_providers.answer: Model selection is inherited from each runtime (explicit model choices applied at start/resume; no CCCC model catalog or guessing). actor --model-label is a human-declared label CCCC does not check or use to launch. ChatGPT Web uses GPT-5.x chats via the bound conversation.

custom_adapters.answer: custom runtime runs any command; capabilities install from explicit local path, URL or GitHub target with recorded provenance; slash skills dispatch skill: packs.

session_integration.answer: Managed sessions get an agent-scoped MCP server (preflight verified before launch); native user-run Codex/Claude/Pi/OpenCode sessions integrate via MCP plus hooks/plugin/extension; Web models use a remote MCP connector.

mixed_harness_operation.answer: Each agent chooses its own runtime and both managed and connected sessions work in the same Group; workflows document Claude + Codex + Kimi style mixes with a reviewer runtime for diversity.

limitations: Model choice and provider login stay with each runtime; actor model-label is declarative and unchecked.

claims.answer: Agents run on the user own existing subscriptions and logins: connected sessions keep their app process, account, model, approvals and terminal, and CCCC needs no provider API key. Managed agents are launched from the user-installed CLIs. No vendor credits, paid CCCC plans or card exist; per-actor private environment supports different model/API stacks per agent. The only account is the optional free CCCC account for Connect/Reach; local use needs none.

agent_subscriptions.answer: Bring your own agent subscription: managed agents launch from installed, signed-in CLIs; connected sessions keep their own conversation, account, model and approvals; ChatGPT/Grok voice reuse their CLI logins with no extra API key.

api_accounts.answer: Runtime accounts stay runtime-side (CLI logins, ChatGPT sign-in + remote MCP connector, Google credential for NotebookLM, IM bot tokens). CCCC keeps IM credentials and actor secrets but owns no provider billing account.

vendor_credits.answer: Subscriptions, vendor credits: bounded search of the site, docs, account pages and CLI reference found no vendor credits; automation notices may use model credits via the user own runtime logins.

local_models.answer: Subscriptions, local_models: no local-model runtime or guide was located; whether an arbitrary local-model CLI works through custom is unproven in the checked sources.

account_switching.answer: Runtime-only actor secrets give each agent different model/API stacks; ChatGPT connector credentials are agent-specific; multiple runtime logins coexist across agents in one Group.

vendor_account_requirement.answer: Local CCCC works with no account and no sign-in; the free CCCC account is only needed for Connect and managed Remote Access, and direct Connect pairs need no account at all.

provider_restrictions.answer: Documented runtime restrictions: Antigravity cannot join as a connected session, Web models need public HTTPS + pairing, DeepSeek is developer preview, managed agents may bypass approvals (review commands first), test boundaries Linux/WSL only.

limitations: No CCCC-side billing or credits; all inference spend stays on the user runtime accounts.

claims.answer: Install (shell/PowerShell/pip/Docker/source), run cccc, create a Group, add an installed signed-in agent and send the first message. Any local directory attaches as a scope with no Git requirement; Git clones get read-only diffs (CCCC never stages/commits). Prerequisites are an agent CLI install + sign-in (plus Node 24 for JS code mode, Xvfb for projected browsers). Managed cloud does not exist; a BYO VPS path runs headless under a supervisor with LAN/tunnel/Tailscale/Reach access (Reach helper Linux/macOS only).

first_task_setup.answer: Install, cccc launch, create Group, add agent from detected runtimes, start Group, send message; CLI (attach/actor add/group start/send) and Web (sidebar create, + add agent) flows both documented with troubleshooting.

no_git.answer: Onboarding, no_git: cccc attach works on any local directory and a Group without a project folder simply has no backlog; no Git requirement is stated in the install/launch flows.

local_git_without_remote.answer: Local Git repos work: Files shows untracked/ignored files, Changes lists working-tree/staged/conflicts/untracked items with diffs; a created BACKLOG.md is excluded via the clone-local exclude, not .gitignore.

hosted_git.answer: Works inside a hosted-git clone like any checkout (agents use git/runtime tools there); no hosted-git-specific onboarding or integration is documented.

prerequisite_guidance.answer: At least one supported agent runtime CLI installed and signed in; source builds need Rust 1.88+/Node 24/npm/Python 3.11+; MCP JavaScript code mode needs Node on the host; projected browsers need Xvfb/x11vnc on Linux.

managed_cloud_setup.answer: Onboarding, managed_cloud_setup: bounded search found no managed-cloud compute offering; Remote Access publishes the user own machine and explicitly uploads neither repository nor ledger.

byo_vps_onboarding.answer: Headless/server/container operation under a service manager with LAN binding, tunnels, Tailscale or Reach; Reach install/publish is a Linux/macOS preview needing an Admin token, and its Windows helper is not in this release.

limitations: No managed-cloud option; Reach remote publishing is a Linux/macOS preview.

claims.answer: A complete product-owned CLI plus MCP surfaces (daemon tools over stdio for agents; Python/TypeScript/Rust SDK clients for integrators; documented Web API endpoints), but no generic public REST API with stability promises and no generic outgoing webhooks. Create/inspect/steer/stop/review run through CLI, MCP, Web and IM; auth is loopback-local principal plus Admin Access Tokens for non-local use.

cli.answer: Full cccc CLI: daemon/groups/actors/messaging/inbox/ledger/IM/space/setup/update/web/mcp with JSON doctor output and documented env vars; the terminal panel adds an interactive command menu.

api.answer: Documented Web API endpoints exist (push config/subscription, capabilities allowlist, files/AGENTS.md, backlog, group operations) but no versioned public REST API with stability guarantees is stated.

sdk.answer: Separate cccc-sdk with Python, TypeScript and Rust clients connecting to a running cccc; daemon owns lifecycle/delivery, SDK carries no daemon.

mcp_server.answer: cccc mcp serves collaboration tools over stdio; agents see a compact core (bootstrap/help/inbox/messaging/files/context/coordination/task/connect) with capability-managed expansion packs.

webhooks.answer: Programmable access, webhooks: bounded search found no generic outgoing webhooks; provider-side Webhook Routines (Grok Bot) and ChatGPT event tasks are runtime-specific inbound mechanisms.

operations.answer: Create/inspect/steer/stop/review via CLI (groups/actor/send/reply/deliver/inbox/tail/ledger search), MCP (group/actor/messaging/automation/terminal/debug), Web run controls and IM commands.

authentication.answer: Local loopback gets a passwordless in-memory administrator principal; non-local clients need an Admin Access Token (account linking initializes one); IM credentials via env-var references preferred.

stability.answer: Daemon IPC is a versioned contract (CCCS/daemon-IPC standards docs); Web API/MCP evolution follows release notes with upgrade caveats, but no API stability/SLA statement exists.

limitations: No versioned public REST API or generic webhooks; automation-capable surface is CLI/MCP/Web/IM.

claims.answer: Capabilities install as mounted skill packs from explicit local paths, URLs or GitHub targets with provenance; slash skills dispatch them. CCCC sets up its own MCP into most runtimes itself (prompt-assisted where the runtime requires it) and governs tool visibility with a foreman/user allowlist. No external-MCP consumption by CCCC itself and no plugin framework beyond capability packs were established; repo instructions import through the AGENTS.md editor, watched instruction files and cccc_file.

mcp_client.answer: External tools, mcp_client: bounded inspection of the docs and daemon/MCP sources found CCCC exposing MCP to agents (server side) but no consumption of third-party MCP servers by CCCC itself.

plugins.answer: Capability packs mount/enable/pin/block per group or globally; third-party sources are discoverable by default with a conservative safety mode. No general plugin framework beyond capability packs is documented.

custom_tools.answer: Custom runtime runs any command; finite MCP shell/Git tools, local code execution (web_model), repo inspection tools and snippets/automation actions extend behavior; cccc_code_exec/cccc_shell exist behind capability use.

instructions_import.answer: AGENTS.md editor in Project Context, watched instruction files (AGENTS/CLAUDE variants) with change nudges, protocol reference customization, skill/capability import with provenance.

authentication.answer: IM tokens as env-var references or literals (env preferred); actor/runtime secrets stored daemon-side with key-metadata-only reads; ChatGPT/Google credentials via their own sign-in flows.

permission_scope.answer: Foreman/peer/user permission matrix kernel-enforced by the daemon; capability allowlist overlays group vs global scope; workspace+Group permission checks on file/media reads; exhibit read-only mode.

integration_owner.answer: CCCC-owned per-session MCP setup for most runtimes with preflight repair; Cursor/Kilo/Antigravity use prompt-assisted contracts and session-owned MCP, inheriting runtime-side setup.

limitations: Capability governance is tool visibility, not process sandboxing; no third-party MCP consumption.

claims.answer: No installable desktop or native mobile client ships: access is the React+TypeScript+Vite+Tailwind+xterm Web UI in desktop/mobile browsers (installable as a standalone-display PWA) plus the Rust CLI/daemon and terminal panel. Implementation evidence is pinned source: web/package.json dependency set, PWA manifest, Rust workspace members. No hybrid wrappers were found.

desktop_implementation.answer: Client implementation, desktop_implementation: bounded search found no desktop client implementation; desktop access is the browser Web UI plus the native CLI executable.

mobile_implementation.answer: No native iOS/Android implementation; the mobile surface is the responsive Web UI with phone layouts plus the standalone-display PWA manifest (Home Screen use).

hybrids.answer: Client implementation, hybrids: bounded source inspection found no Electron/Tauri/React-Native/wrapper shells; installers ship the native Rust executable plus the web bundle.

implementation_evidence.answer: Pinned source evidence: web/package.json (react, xterm, tailwind, vite, typescript), web/public/manifest.webmanifest, Rust workspace crates (daemon/web/runtime/cli/mcp), install.ps1/install.sh shipping native executables.

limitations: Browser+PWA+CLI only; no native or hybrid clients.

claims.answer: Groups, tasks and backlog entries are created natively by humans (composer, CLI, Web) with durable task/event IDs, and the Group ledger is the authoritative record for product-owned work. There is no import from Linear/GitHub/Jira or other external trackers and no chat/Git triggers; CCCC-to-CCCC Connect relays messages between instances rather than syncing trackers, so no external round-trip exists.

local_creation.answer: Groups created in Web sidebar or via cccc attach/group create; tasks created in the board editor, from backlog topics, or linked via tracked-send with owner/outcome.

prompt_intake.answer: Composer messages with @mentions, CLI send/tracked-send, and IM /send take work in as chat addressed to foreman/peers/agents.

external_import.answer: Intake, external_import: bounded inspection of guides, CLI reference and daemon ops found no import from external trackers; the only file-based intake is the project BACKLOG.md.

chat_git_triggers.answer: Intake, chat_git_triggers: no chat triggers or git-event triggers start work; automation triggers are interval/cron/one-time rules only.

authoritative_tracker.answer: The Group ledger plus context/tasks store is the authoritative record (append-only events, ctxv revisions); no external tracker is required or designated.

stable_ids.answer: Durable task IDs, ledger event IDs, backlog hidden entry IDs and CLI idempotency keys keep identity across restarts, copies and renames.

sync.answer: Intake, sync: no two-way sync with external trackers exists; Connect relays messages/replies/files between CCCC instances with each keeping its own state.

supported_edits.answer: Tasks edit in Web/CLI/agent tools with conflict guards; external-tracker edits do not apply since no external tracker is integrated.

external_roundtrips.answer: Intake, external_roundtrips: no operations require a trip back to an external tracker; repository work happens through the workspace and runtimes.

limitations: Self-contained issue tracking; no external tracker integration of any kind.

claims.answer: Tasks carry title, status, assignee, priority, outcome, checklist, notes, subtasks and handoff/blocking links, editable in the Web board, CLI-tracked sends and agent tools with optimistic-concurrency revisions. Plans amend freely mid-run, link to backlog topics and handoffs, and persist across restarts in the daemon-owned context store.

plans.answer: Tasks with goal/focus/coordination brief, outcome, checklist and notes; tracked-send creates task + linked delegation message with owner and outcome.

acceptance_criteria.answer: Outcome field plus task-type requirements and per-item checklist states record what done means; a done task without an outcome gets a suggestion to add one.

editors.answer: Web task editor, CLI tracked-send fields (--checklist/--notes/--task-priority), backlog entry editing, and agent task tools all mutate the same store.

revisions.answer: ctxv optimistic revisions with expected-version saves; conflicting saves are refused with the edits kept for copying; import preserves event IDs.

implementation_links.answer: Backlog topics link to tasks made from them (task shows topic title), handoffs/parents/blocking tasks sit under Advanced details, outcomes write back to topics.

amendment.answer: Tasks move across Planned/Active/Done, subtasks/checklists/outcomes edit in place, backlog topics move/close/reopen; type requirements describe completeness but never block a change.

restart_persistence.answer: Tasks/context persist in CCCC_HOME context store across daemon restarts; imported groups start idle with actors stopped and history intact.

claims.answer: Tasks form a parent/subtask tree with assignees and blocked_by/waiting-on attention states derived into blocked badges (recomputed, cf. fix #201), linked to backlog topics that outlive them. No epic entity, readiness gate or dependency enforcement exists: type requirements never block a change and Mail never starts an agent. No rigid workflow is required by design.

epics.answer: Hierarchy, epics: bounded inspection found no epic entity with rollup state; backlog topics group ideas but carry no status rollup or dispatch semantics.

hierarchy.answer: Parent tasks with subtasks (progress counts of direct non-archived subtasks), backlog sections/topics nesting ideas; arbitrary-depth nesting beyond one subtask level is unproven.

blockers.answer: blocked_by/waiting-on fields with blocked/waiting attention filters and badges; a task whose waited-on tasks complete stops counting as blocked (#201).

readiness.answer: Waiting/on-hold states surface via attention filters and Waiting for you; no dispatch readiness gate was located (Mail does not start an agent).

enforcement.answer: Hierarchy, enforcement: task-type requirements describe completeness but never block a change; blockers are displayed/derived, not dispatch-enforced.

state_propagation.answer: Status columns, attention badges and Waiting-for-you counts propagate state across the board; cross-task propagation is limited to derived blocked states.

task_to_epic.answer: Backlog topics persist while tasks complete (finishing never closes the topic) with task links and outcome write-back, but no epic promotion primitive exists.

identity_retention.answer: Task IDs, backlog hidden entry IDs and event IDs survive edits, moves, renames, restarts and group copies; concurrent saves conflict instead of forking identity.

workflow_constraints.answer: No rigid preselected workflow is required: a quick send needs no preset, and CCCC is explicitly not a DAG workflow orchestrator.

limitations: Derived (not enforced) blockers; no epics, gates or mandatory workflows.

claims.answer: Repository instructions live in the workspace AGENTS.md editor plus watched AGENTS/CLAUDE variants with change nudges; project docs in Files; working memory in Tasks/context/Agent State and the NotebookLM work/memory notebooks; skills as installable capability packs with self-evolving candidates surfaced per Group. Provenance is ledger attribution with staleness marks; correction/deletion run through editors, archive/delete and version conflicts; no spec-drift detection exists.

instructions.answer: AGENTS.md editor at the workspace root, watched AGENTS.override/AGENTS/CLAUDE variants with one-line change nudges on next delivery, optional team re-read notification; each runtime keeps its own discovery/precedence.

skills.answer: Skills panel shows self-evolving candidates from the Group; capabilities install from explicit sources and dispatch via skill: packs; full candidate lifecycle (promote/retire) is unstated.

project_docs.answer: Workspace Files browser with Markdown/Mermaid/CSV/PDF viewers, Presentation slots, pinned documents and message attachments all read the same workspace.

memory.answer: Agent State latest reports with timestamps/staleness, context brief/decisions/handoffs, NotebookLM memory notebook via explicit ingest; legacy memory files are retained in copies but no dedicated search/update tool remains.

scope.answer: Group vs instance settings, per-group protocol reference, per-workspace AGENTS.md, per-actor secrets; Chet reads every Group as context but forwarding/isolation between Groups is instruction-only, not enforced.

provenance.answer: Ledger records sender (by) per event; Agent State shows timestamps and staleness; task saves are versioned. Citation-grade provenance of external knowledge is unstated.

correction.answer: Tasks, backlog topics, AGENTS.md and files edit in place with conflict guards; automation/snippet and guidance documents are user-editable.

deletion.answer: Delete for never-started planned tasks, archive otherwise, pin/message removal, backlog close/reopen, capability uninstall, account/device deletion flows.

freshness.answer: Staleness shown on Agent State and instruction nudges on file change; no systematic freshness/retention policy for memory beyond compaction/retention windows.

takeover_continuity.answer: Same Group continues from another device via remote access or Connect; managed agents resume saved conversations (PATH-change improvements in 0.4.55); native sessions rejoin with recovery guidance.

limitations: Chet cross-group context is instruction-level, not isolated; memory search/update tooling retired.

claims.answer: Agents read the workspace through Files, message attachments (images/video/PDF/audio), Mermaid/PDF viewers, repo inspection tools and explicit NotebookLM ingestion (files, pasted text, URLs, YouTube, Drive). Bounded repo inspection and scoped editing exist for web runtimes. No product-wide code indexing, citation model, conflict detection or review-time enforcement was established.

code_search.answer: Bounded repository inspection via web_model runtime and cccc_repo inspection tools; no product-wide semantic code search was located.

indexing.answer: Architecture, indexing: bounded inspection of the pinned tree (crates/*/src, web/src, docs/**) finds no repository-indexing service; retrieval is tool- and attachment-scoped, NotebookLM ingestion is explicit per item.

external_knowledge.answer: NotebookLM work/memory notebook binding with explicit file/URL/YouTube/Drive ingestion, query and jobs via agent/CLI tools; web URL content reachable the same way.

multimodal_inputs.answer: Image/video/PDF/audio attachments with viewers, Mermaid diagrams, before/after screenshots in reviews, live voice transcripts and documents via Chet/Secretary.

freshness.answer: Reload paths (Reload file, refresh, re-ingest) and staleness marks exist; source freshness tracking and enforcement are unstated.

access_scope.answer: Reads stay in the active workspace with Group permission checks; symlinks/outside-workspace targets disabled with reasons; exhibit mode hides Files.

api_retrieval.answer: cccc_file/cccc_file_send/cccc_repo/message-history/space-query tooling plus ledger search give agents and users programmatic retrieval.

citations.answer: Quotes, references, message links and file-path mentions carry provenance; no formal citation/conflict model exists.

conflict_detection.answer: Architecture awareness, conflict_detection: bounded inspection found no architectural conflict detection; concurrent task saves conflict, which is edit concurrency, not knowledge conflicts.

review_enforcement.answer: Architecture awareness, review_enforcement: no review-time conformance enforcement exists; review outcomes are recorded as messages, not gates.

limitations: Retrieval is tool- and file-scoped; no index, citations model or enforcement.

claims.answer: A complete native task system: create/edit/discuss/prioritize/assign/search/filter/archive/reopen in the board, idea parking in the project BACKLOG.md, explicit dispatch via tracked-send, durable Planned/Active/Done states and task/session separation with per-task metadata. No labels/tags, no epic views, no external tracker: nothing external is needed or integrated.

create.answer: Tasks created in the board editor, from backlog topics (Create task), or linked via tracked-send; backlog topics and ideas created in the file view.

edit.answer: Title/status/assignee/priority/outcome/checklist/notes/subtasks edit with version-conflict guards; backlog entries edit in place with file-hash fencing.

discuss.answer: Messages with @mentions, reply/quote/forward, review tables and outcome discussion carry task discussion; Waiting for you collects open questions.

prioritize.answer: Per-task priority field plus attention filters (blocked/waiting/handoff/unassigned) and Waiting-for-you ordering surface what matters.

label.answer: Native issues, label: bounded inspection of the board editor, task ops and CLI found priority/assignee/attention but no label/tag field.

assign.answer: Assignee per task, @foreman/@peers addressing, tracked-send --assignee/--waiting-on/--handoff-to delegation fields.

search.answer: Board search with match quotes plus daemon ledger search (-q text, sender/recipient/kind/time filters) across history.

filter.answer: Status columns, attention filters, sender filters, assignee filters and message tabs (Waiting/All/Pinned/User-related).

archive.answer: Archive for finished tasks (Restore returns prior status); backlog Closed section for finished topics with Reopen.

reopen.answer: Restore archived tasks, Reopen closed backlog topics, resume stopped groups and restart agents on new or resumed sessions.

project_epic_views.answer: Board columns plus per-group sidebar status cover projects; no epic rollup or cross-group portfolio view exists.

idea_parking.answer: BACKLOG.md holds long-lived topics/ideas beside Tasks with entry-to-task links and outcome write-back; tasks work without one.

explicit_dispatch.answer: tracked-send creates a task and sends one linked delegation with owner and outcome; automation one-time rules dispatch operations.

task_session_separation.answer: Tasks (durable records) are distinct from agents/sessions (runtimes); several agents can attach to work on tasks and sessions restart independently.

metadata.answer: Status/assignee/priority/outcome/checklist/notes/subtasks/handoff/blocking/type; no labels, estimates or custom fields.

durable_states.answer: Planned/Active/Done/Archived with transitions, restore semantics and daemon-persisted context across restarts.

external_tracker_requirement.answer: No external tracker is required or used: tasks, ledger, context and files all live under CCCC_HOME; IDE/GitHub/Linear round-trips do not exist.

limitations: No labels/tags, estimates or epic views; single-product tracking only.

claims.answer: Agents share the same durable task IDs humans use: list/get via cccc_task-class tools, create via tracked delegation, update with optimistic-concurrency batches under foreman/peer role gates, assign/state/subtask/result through context ops, all visible in the Web board with ledger attribution. Self-claim and agent-set dependencies are only partly established; conflicts surface as explicit task_conflict errors.

shared_ids.answer: Task/event/backlog IDs are identical across Web, CLI, MCP and IM; agents quote them in replies and links.

read.answer: Agents read tasks via task list/get tools, message history and context projections with attention lists and counts.

create.answer: tracked-send creates a task plus its linked delegation message; backlog-sourced creation and CLI task fields cover human creation; agent creation flows through the same daemon ops.

update.answer: Validated batch mutations with compare-and-swap revisions; conflicting saves are refused with edits preserved for copying.

claim.answer: Assignees record ownership and foreman assigns work; agent self-claim of unassigned tasks is not separately established.

assign.answer: Foreman (and user) may add/manage actors and set assignees; tracked-send carries --assignee/--waiting-on/--handoff-to.

state_changes.answer: Status moves (Planned/Active/Done/Archived) through board, CLI and task ops with version guards.

dependencies.answer: blocked_by/waiting-on fields derive blocked attention; whether agents may set them via tools (vs Web) is not separately established.

children.answer: Subtasks with progress counts under Advanced details; backlog topics parent linked tasks.

results.answer: Outcomes, checklists, notes and reply evidence recorded per task; completion evidence stays in the ledger.

human_visibility.answer: Board, messages, Waiting for you and Agent State reflect agent writes immediately with live updates.

attribution.answer: Every ledger event carries its sender; task/editor actions attribute to user, foreman or peer actors.

permissions.answer: Daemon RBAC: peers manage only self, foreman manages any actor; task ops are role-gated; capability allowlist overlays group/global scope.

conflicts.answer: Concurrent mutations fail closed with task_conflict errors naming the change; idempotency keys prevent double-apply.

limitations: Agent self-claim and agent-set dependencies only partly established.

claims.answer: Long-lived requirements persist in the project BACKLOG.md (topics outlive tasks with outcome write-back) and in AGENTS.md guidance; both are human-editable with version/hash guards. Agents write outcomes and notes and read topics/files via tools, with later retrieval through ledger search and context. No formal requirement objects, approval records or drift detection exist.

persistent_requirements.answer: Backlog topics and AGENTS.md persist across tasks/releases as ordinary versioned files; no dedicated requirement records with status exist.

human_edits.answer: Backlog entries, AGENTS.md, tasks and guidance documents edit in place with conflict fencing.

agent_edits.answer: Agents record outcomes/notes and ingest sources via tools; direct agent edits to backlog/AGENTS.md files are possible through file tools but requirement-level authorship is not separately established.

revisions.answer: Whole-file SHA fencing for backlog edits, ctxv revisions for tasks, ledger history for everything; conflicting writes are refused, not merged.

approvals.answer: User answers to agent questions are recorded decisions; no formal approval records or approval rules on specs exist.

implementation_links.answer: Topic-to-task links, task handoff/blocking links, outcome write-back to topics, message/event links.

later_retrieval.answer: Ledger search, message history, context projections and file reads retrieve prior requirements during later work.

drift_detection.answer: Living specs, drift_detection: bounded inspection found instruction-file change nudges only; no specification-drift detection or conformance re-checks.

review_integration.answer: Reviews happen in chat with tables/evidence and outcomes recorded; no formal review gate binds specs to delivery.

limitations: File-based persistence, not a requirements database; no drift detection or approval records.

claims.answer: Several agents run concurrently in a Group and several Groups run side by side; the sidebar, terminal panel and status counts show running, waiting, failed and finished work across them. No concurrency quotas are documented; observed-concurrency evidence is limited to status/running counts rather than measured parallelism.

concurrent_sessions.answer: Multiple agents per Group plus multiple Groups; terminal view pages up to four agents; start/stop per agent or per Group.

concurrent_tasks.answer: Planned/Active/Done tasks coexist with several agents working in parallel; tracked-send fans work out with owners.

quotas.answer: Parallelism, quotas: bounded search of docs, CLI reference and daemon sources found no documented concurrency quotas or limits.

observed_concurrency.answer: RUNNING counts, status dots, activity rings and progress bubbles show live work; no measured concurrency figures are published.

status_visibility.answer: Sidebar Group rows with status and Waiting-for-you counts, terminal panel status dots, Group pages with task-state counts, /status and cccc groups/actor list.

limitations: No quotas; concurrency visibility is status-level, not measured.

claims.answer: Users and the foreman assign and route work (@mentions, default_send_to policy, tracked-send ownership); peers manage only themselves under daemon RBAC. Dispatch is guarded by idempotency keys and single-writer rules. No queues and no duplicate-prevention beyond idempotency were established.
